story.title: Infant Rescued After Being Buried Alive in Dog Crate in South Carolina
story.summary: An 11-month-old baby was rescued after being buried alive in a dog crate for approximately 24 hours in South Carolina. The child was found near his father's home, clinging to life and crying. Authorities reported that a towel wrapped around the crate created an air pocket, which likely helped the infant survive. The baby is currently receiving care in a hospital.

explore_lenses.label: How did searchers locate Koah Sharpe?
explore_lenses.title: The search narrowed near his grandfather’s home
explore_lenses.summary: Authorities say the search shifted from a countywide missing-child effort to a wooded area near the home of Michael Comer’s father, where searchers noticed recently disturbed ground. The rescue followed a multi-agency search after Comer was arrested without the infant present.

claims.text: The Lexington County Sheriff’s Department said investigators believed Koah Sharpe was taken by his father on Monday, November 9, 2026; Comer was arrested late that night on a burglary charge, but the child was not with him.
Sheriff Jay Koon said searchers found disturbed dirt about 50 yards from the grandfather’s house and heard the infant crying as they began digging.
The initial search involved Lexington County deputies, fire service personnel, SLED, FBI and ATF agents, according to the sheriff’s department.

explore_lenses.label: Why did the child survive underground?
explore_lenses.title: Officials cite the crate’s towel and a shallow burial
explore_lenses.summary: The sheriff’s account identifies conditions that may have made survival possible, but it is not a medical conclusion. The child was taken to a hospital immediately after being recovered.

claims.text: Sheriff Koon said Koah was found in a small dog crate wrapped in a towel and that the towel probably created an air pocket; he estimated the child had been underground for about 24 hours.
Koon also said the hole was shallow, a condition he cited alongside the towel when discussing the child’s survival.
The infant was transported to a hospital after the rescue; no detailed medical condition or prognosis had been publicly released in the reporting consulted.

explore_lenses.title: Prosecutors are reviewing possible additional charges
explore_lenses.summary: As of November 11, 2026, Comer was being held on a burglary charge, while investigators and prosecutors assessed whether the alleged conduct surrounding the child warranted further charges. An arrest or allegation is not a conviction.

story_report.summary: An 11-month-old infant was rescued in rural South Carolina after searchers found him buried in a small dog crate near his father’s home, about 24 hours after he was reported missing. Sheriff Jay Koon said searchers heard the child crying after locating disturbed dirt and began digging. The child was taken to a hospital after the rescue. Koon said a towel wrapped around the crate likely created an air pocket, and that the shallow hole may also have aided the infant’s survival.

sections.heading: Search Mobilized Multiple Law Enforcement Agencies
sections.body: The Lexington County Sheriff’s Department said investigators believed Koah Sharpe had been taken by his father on Monday, Nov. 9, 2026. The department said Michael Comer was arrested late that night on a burglary charge, but the child was not with him. Lexington County deputies, fire service personnel, and agents from SLED, the FBI and ATF participated in the initial search.

sections.heading: Investigators Review Potential Additional Charges
sections.body: The sheriff’s department publicly confirmed Comer’s burglary arrest, while its missing-child announcement did not list a charge tied to Koah’s disappearance. Koon said investigators were working with the solicitor’s office to determine whether additional charges would be filed. Any further counts, bond proceedings and court dates will depend on investigators’ evidence and prosecutors’ charging decisions.

related_stories.title: 74-Year-Old Kidnapper Escapes House Arrest in Argentina
related_stories.summary: Leonardo Bertulazzi, a 74-year-old former member of the Red Brigades, escaped from house arrest in Buenos Aires, Argentina. He was awaiting extradition to Italy to serve a 27-year prison sentence. Authorities confirmed his escape, which reportedly involved him using a harness to abseil from a balcony.

related_stories.title: Storm Charles Forces Flight Cancellations and School Closures in Portugal
related_stories.summary: Portugal has canceled over 300 flights and closed schools as Storm Charles impacts the region. Authorities are taking extensive precautions following previous criticisms regarding their response to earlier storms. In neighboring Spain, over 3,000 people have been evacuated due to the risk of flooding from heavy rains and potential dam overflow.

related_stories.title: State Funeral Held for 69 Victims of Train Crash in Toledo
related_stories.summary: A state funeral was held at Toledo Cathedral on November 10 for the 69 victims of a high-speed train collision near Urda on October 28. King Felipe VI and Queen Letizia attended the ceremony, where candles were lit in memory of those who lost their lives in the tragic accident.
